evidence.field: 听 entry; current structural analysis and current senses
evidence.text: The entry for 听 tīng identifies it as left–right structured and analyzes it as 从口、斤声. It lists ordinary hearing/listening and related senses such as accepting, obeying, allowing, and governing, without marking these as obsolete. This independently supports the current visible 口-left / 斤-right split and present-day sense evidence; it does not establish that the sound role arose when 听 was adopted for 聽.
evidence.title: 听 tīng、yǐn - 汉典

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Ministry of Education, Taiwan
evidence.field: B00294 听; readings and sense distinctions
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes yǐn ‘smiling appearance’, with the received Shuowen analysis from 口 with 斤 as phonetic, from tīng and tìng readings listed as variants of 聽. It cites Sima Xiangru’s Shanglin fu and a Tang text for the smiling sense. The record therefore supports treating these as distinct uses/readings; the cited examples do not establish the first occurrence.
evidence.title: [B00294] 听 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》, Ministry of Education, Taiwan
evidence.field: A03282-011 听 (聽); cited vernacular use and standardized correspondence
evidence.text: The 聽 record lists 听 as a variant, cites 宋元以來俗字譜 for vernacular forms, and gives the standardized correspondence 聽作听. This supports use of 听 for 聽 by the Song–Yuan source tradition and the standardized simplified counterpart relation, but does not specify when the vernacular use began or how it arose.

evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692; direct scan inspection
evidence.field: PDF p. 96, printed p. 84; right-column 听 entry. Scan path /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0096/source.png; decoded-RGB pixel SHA-256 69168e4fc33daaa019d2fcb5a92db744d480dc4be542c17c75f20e325b9e9b2c. Inspected crop bounds (1500, 300, 2950, 2300).
evidence.text: The printed page gives yǐn on the 听 headword line and tīng beneath it. The paragraph assigns ‘smiling appearance’ and 口-plus-斤 phonosemantic analysis to the yǐn entry, then says 听 has been a simplified form of 聽 since the Yuan. The scan agrees with the corpus text and confirms printed page 84. It does not state that the historical sound analysis explains the simplified form’s adoption.

evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692; direct scan inspection
evidence.field: PDF p. 1062, printed p. 1047, 聽 entry; its paragraph continues in the left column of PDF p. 1063, printed p. 1048. Scan paths /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-1062/source.png and page-1063/source.png; pixel SHA-256 values fe34de73317b7c55cc85ba8a55d314cfe2317557f969e16244dd46481d12b683 and ddcb3221267a8835c75a41d8895db067cea12b2eb86c34adffe4c298f6dbecbb. Inspected crops p.1062 bounds (1450, 2500, 2950, 4050), p.1063 bounds (80, 100, 1650, 1050).
evidence.text: The 聽 entry’s historical sequence is labeled 商, 西周, 戰國, 說文小篆, 漢, then clerical forms. The author analyzes the oracle-bone and bronze forms as associative, with ear and mouth representing speech received by the ear, and describes the received Shuowen account as adding 悳 as a sound element. The continuation discusses extensions from hearing to accepting/obeying, inquiry/governance, and waiting. It then says 聽 is now simplified to 听, separately identified with the Shuowen 口-plus-斤 analysis and smiling sense. These are the author’s analyses; the scan does not establish every proposed historical relationship.
